name: Christoph Hurni
role: President of the First Civil Law Division, Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland (président de la première Cour de droit civil)
party: Grünliberale Partei (GLP), as published by the Federal Supreme Court
bio: Christoph Hurni, born in Bern in 1979, is a judge of the Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland and, as of October 2026, president of its First Civil Law Division. He was elected a federal judge by the United Federal Assembly on 23 September 2020, on a party's proposal, as Swiss federal judges are; the Court lists his party as the GLP (Green Liberal Party). After law studies in Bern and Bologna, a doctorate (2007), admission to the Bern bar (2009) and a habilitation (2017), he was a clerk at the Federal Supreme Court from 2008 to 2017 and a judge of the Bern High Court, part-time from 2013 to 2017 and then from 2017 to 2020 as an ordinary judge presiding over its Second Civil Chamber; the Court's biography also lists him as a titular professor at the University of Zurich. In September 2023 he was a member of the Second Criminal Law Division panel in cases 7B_15/2021 and 7B_16/2021, whose statement that a lower court could take into account the relatively short duration of a rape in sentencing was disavowed by the Court in a separate 2024 judgment; the collegial judgment does not identify the author of that passage or how each judge voted.
